subject: feat(github-actions): enable automatic PyPi release on publish
message:
feat(github-actions): enable automatic PyPi release on publish

This commit enables automatic PyPi release for the 'pyvespa' library when a new release is published on GitHub. Previously, the release workflow was disabled, but this change now triggers the release process when a new release is published.

The key changes are:
- Modify the release trigger to listen for 'published' events instead of 'workflow_dispatch'
- Add an environment variable 'RELEASE_REF' to ensure the version is available, even if the 'GITHUB_REF' variable is not set correctly
- Update the version extraction logic to use the 'RELEASE_REF' variable instead of 'GITHUB_REF'

Add adaptive throttling for async requests

  error rates to prevent 504s and connection resets

Fixes issue with overloading Vespa apps configured with expensive
operations (large embedding models).

Migrated both synchronous and asynchronous HTTP clients to use the
httpr library for improved performance and consistency.

Changes:
- VespaSync: Migrated from requests.Session to httpr.Client
  - Moved compression logic from CustomHTTPAdapter to _prepare_request_body
  - Moved 429 retry logic to _request_with_retry helper method
  - Added _prepare_mtls_cert for combining cert+key files
  - Removed CustomHTTPAdapter class entirely

- VespaAsync: Migrated from httpx.AsyncClient to httpr.AsyncClient
  - Simplified timeout handling (now uses float instead of httpx.Timeout)
  - Added backward compatibility for httpx.Timeout with deprecation warning
  - Updated attribute name from httpx_client to httpr_client

- Deployment: Updated HTTP client usage in deployment.py
  - Replaced httpx.Client with httpr.Client
  - Constructed full URLs (httpr doesn't have base_url parameter)

- Dependencies: Added httpr to pyproject.toml

- Tests: Updated all unit tests to mock httpr.Client/AsyncClient
  - Created create_mock_httpr_response() helper function
  - Updated 13 tests with @patch decorators for httpr mocking
  - Fixed VespaAsync tests to reflect new timeout and client attributes
  - Updated connection reuse tests (http_client, _owns_client)

subject: test(models): handle HF HTTP 429 in URL validation test
message:
test(models): handle HF HTTP 429 in URL validation test

The HF model URL validation runs as a unit test across a 16-job
matrix (4 OS x 4 Python), all making live unauthenticated requests
to huggingface.co. The concurrent load triggers HTTP 429 rate
limiting, which fails CI even though the URLs are valid.

  still failing on genuinely broken URLs (404, etc.).
- Send an HF_TOKEN auth header during validation when available;
  authenticated requests have far higher rate limits.
- Pass HF_TOKEN to the unit-test workflow so the auth path is
  effective in CI.

subject: fix(mteb): set maxHits in query profile to fix HTTP 500 on retrieval
message:
fix(mteb): set maxHits in query profile to fix HTTP 500 on retrieval

MTEB retrieval queries request hits=top_k (up to ~1000), which exceeds
Vespa's default maxHits of 400. common_query_params passed maxHits as a
runtime query parameter, but Vespa does not allow that ("maxHits must be
specified in a query profile") - so every query returned HTTP 500 and all
profiles scored NDCG@10 = 0.0, failing the cloud integration test.

- create_hybrid_package now attaches a default query profile with
  maxHits=10000 so hits=top_k requests are accepted.
- Drop maxHits from common_query_params (cannot be set per-request).
- Log the Vespa error body (not just the status code) on query failure,
  which is what made this diagnosable.

Verified against Vespa Cloud: test passes with semantic=0.62092,
bm25=0.52063, fusion=0.60338, atan_norm=0.62851, norm_linear=0.64687.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
